one_line: Product handled from 0:00 under a claim card, a text-free demo, then one DM ask held at the end.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 top-down table: a row of round pizza cards, loose white wedges, a child's arm reaching in, the box at lower left. No speech. Text: "ילדים לא משתעממים מללמוד אותיות הם משתעממים מהדרך שבה מלמדים אותן".
q1_hook.why: The claim blames the way letters are taught, so teachers and parents of gan-age children can self-select in the first frame (H1, T3). The game is on screen and being handled from 0:00 (S1). No face or voice opens it (against H4), so the hook rests on text alone (H6).

beats.what: Wide top-down table; the child's arm moves wedges; claim card about boredom
beats.why: Claim and visible game share one frame

beats.what: Same shot; wedges matched onto a letter pizza; card: "בלי להרגיש שהם בכלל לומדים"
beats.why: States the benefit while the game moves

beats.what: Picture wedges (milk bottle, igloo, bicycle, rabbit) pressed onto the pizza; no text
beats.why: A text-free beat lets the activity be read

beats.what: Close-up laminated sheet: a marker circles a balloon, then a door, beside a letter pizza
beats.why: Second activity adds variety, but one action repeats for 9 s

beats.what: Wide pack shot: kit box, finished pizzas, child's hands; CTA text
beats.why: Ends on the product and the single ask

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: A DM ask only ("שלחו לי הודעה"), on screen from 0:20 and in the caption. No question, no save or send prompt.
q2_flow.why: No open loop or payoff, so the Reel leans on constant hand movement and a new activity at 0:11 (R3). The 9 s worksheet stretch repeats one action with no text (R1). It stops right at the CTA with no dead tail, which suits 23 s (R2, E8). Nothing gives a viewer someone to send it to (R5).

q3_cta.what: On screen from 0:20 to the end: "לפרטים על הערכה שלחו לי הודעה 🩷". Caption, last line: "לפרטים על הערכה -שלחו לי הודעה 💌". Not spoken (no speech).
q3_cta.why: One ask, a DM, repeated on screen and in the caption (C1), placed after both activities have been shown (C6), with a stated purpose: details (C2). It is not spoken, and with no price or keyword the viewer cannot tell what the reply will bring (C6).

q4_shown.what: Cards, wedges and the box on screen from 0:00 (box large again 0:20 to 0:22); a child's hands matching wedges 0:00 to 0:11, circling pictures on a laminated sheet 0:11 to 0:19; finished pizzas at the end. No face, price or result.
q4_shown.why: The product is handled from the first second (S1) and carried by hands alone with no face (S4, S5). The kit's name shows only briefly, at the start and end, so the brand stays light (C7). It shows use, not a result or a person vouching, so the "learn without noticing" claim is untested (S6).

q5_edit.what: 4 shots in 23 s (about 5.7 s each), straight cuts at about 4.7, 11.2 and 20.4 s, handheld, no speed change seen. Text cards 0:00-0:03, 0:05-0:08 and 0:20 to the end; none between. No speech. Ends on a held pack shot.
q5_edit.why: Text and motion arrive in the first second (E1), but the first cut is at about 4.7 s and shots run 5 to 9 s, slower than the 2 to 5 s guide (E2). No speech, so sound-on viewers get nothing extra (E4). It stops cleanly at the CTA (E8).

q6_topic.what: A letter-learning game kit for gan-age children, shown as play instead of drilling; it serves teachers and parents who want letter practice that kids enjoy.
q6_topic.why: It speaks to a real preschool concern, learning letters (K6), and the hashtag #הכנהלכיתהא ties it loosely to school start (K7). It has no emotional peak or mini story, so it informs more than it moves (K1, K2). The boredom claim is stated flatly and cannot be checked (K4).

q7_filmed.what: Handheld top-down view over a cream table: wide at 0:00, medium on the wedges, close-up on a laminated worksheet 0:11 to 0:19, wide again at the end. Bright even indoor light, a classroom-like room (blue chairs, shelves). A child's arms and torso only.
q7_filmed.why: Top-down hands at table height show the game the way a viewer would play it (F5, S4), and the worksheet close-up makes the pictures readable (F4). Plain light and a real table look native and sharp (F7), and 9:16 fills the screen (F1). The wide opening makes the cards small.

q8_text.on_screen: White text with a dark outline, no box, centred, roughly 55 to 85 percent down the frame: "ילדים לא משתעממים מללמוד אותיות הם משתעממים מהדרך שבה מלמדים אותן" (0:00-0:03, 4 lines); "עם פיצת האותיות הם משחקים, נהנים ולומדים אותיות בלי להרגיש שהם בכלל לומדים" (0:05-0:08, 5 lines); no text 0:09-0:19; "לפרטים על הערכה שלחו לי הודעה 🩷" (0:20-end).
q8_text.caption: "פיצת האותיות 🍕". About 20 words in 4 short lines: product name, two benefit lines, then the DM ask. No question, 4 hashtags (#גןילדים #פעילותלילדים #גננות #הכנהלכיתהא), no disclosure.
q8_text.why: The text carries the whole message, so it works muted (T1), and the first card is a clear headline (T3). The cards run 4 and 5 lines for about 3 to 4 s each (T5) and sit partly in the bottom 35% (T4). The caption opens with the product name (T7).

weak_points: No voice, face or trust cue; a generic claim with no result shown; no price or way to buy; 4 and 5 line cards low in the frame; 9 s of one repeated worksheet action.
lumebook_takeaway: Film the book from above with hands turning pages, a short claim card in frame one, a held end shot and one DM ask. No child.
not_verified: Audio: the transcript is only "תודה רבה", so there is no speech; music or natural sound cannot be told. Whether she is a teacher or the seller, and the price. The cut at 4.7 s, and a possible extra cut near 0:17 where the framing changes, are not confirmed from 1 s frames. Disclosure: none visible, commercial status unknown.
